independence.command_path: Evaluated after the control request is formed and before any actuator is driven. Cannot be reconfigured through the operator or supervisory path.
independence.limits: Policy thresholds are loaded from configuration at start and are not writable at runtime by any simulated command path.
independence.measurement: Uses the independent level element (configs/process.yaml), modelled on a separate channel from the operator level transmitter and unaffected by sensor.* scenario effects. This independence is a MODELLING ASSUMPTION.

backstop.name: Independent command constraint and high-level trip

rules.description: Any requested level setpoint is clamped into the permitted engineering range regardless of its origin or authorisation.
rules.name: Setpoint absolute clamp

rules.description: Bounds the rate at which the effective setpoint may move, so a single mutated command cannot produce a step change in process target.
rules.name: Setpoint slew limit

rules.description: Denies any pump-run permissive when the INDEPENDENT level element reads at or above the trip level. This is the rule that survives falsification of the operator level transmitter (SCN-003).
rules.name: Independent high-level pump trip

rules.description: Denies the pump-run permissive when the source level is at or below the suction limit, preventing the pump from operating without suction.
rules.name: Dry-run suction interlock

rules.description: Denies a pump start until the configured minimum off time has elapsed, bounding motor start frequency.
rules.name: Anti-cycle minimum off time

conduits.data: Process state read; operator setpoint write. This is the only path on which a control command may travel, and every command crossing it is subject to the engineering backstop.

consequences.description: Process inside the normal operating band, demand fully met, no invariant in a non-OK state.
consequences.name: Normal operation

consequences.description: Process outside the normal band but within safe bounds, a brief service shortfall, or a detected divergence between reported and true telemetry. Operationally noteworthy; mission not impaired.
consequences.name: Minor operational deviation

consequences.description: Delivered flow has fallen materially short of demand for a sustained period. Customers experience reduced pressure and availability.
consequences.name: Service degradation

consequences.description: Delivered flow has fallen below half of demand for a sustained period, or the operational reserve has been lost beyond its tolerance. The critical function CF-001 is not being performed.
consequences.name: Loss of required service

consequences.description: The process has entered a state outside its safe operating envelope: storage above the safe working level, or a pump operating without suction. Equipment damage or loss of containment is now credible.
consequences.name: Unsafe physical state

consequences.description: Loss of containment at scale, or a prolonged unsafe state coincident with loss of the required service. Reserved for outcomes that are not recoverable within the operating period.
consequences.name: Catastrophic mission failure

satisfied_when: no invariant in {INV-001, INV-002, INV-003} is VIOLATED
critical_function.statement: Maintain sufficient water storage to satisfy synthetic demand while keeping the process inside defined safe operating bounds.

invariants.name: Maximum safe tank level
invariants.rationale: Sustained operation above the safe working level risks overtopping the structure and the associated contamination ingress pathway. The limit sits 0.50 m below the physical overflow height so an excursion is observable and recoverable rather than immediately catastrophic.

invariants.name: Minimum operational reserve
invariants.rationale: The reserve volume backs firefighting draw and short-notice demand. Brief excursions during a surge are operationally normal; a sustained excursion is a loss of the required service.

invariants.name: Pump dry-run protection
invariants.rationale: Running a centrifugal pump without suction destroys seals and bearings within minutes. The pump draws current while delivering no flow, so this condition is invisible in a level trend alone.

invariants.name: Command-rate constraint
invariants.rationale: Bounds control action to physically achievable and equipment-safe transitions. Rapid setpoint slew or motor short-cycling is either physically impossible or damaging, and is a signature of automated rather than human command origin.

invariants.name: Telemetry integrity awareness
invariants.rationale: The evidence model must be able to represent a divergence between physical reality and the operator-facing view even while the operator-facing view is wrong. This invariant is the reason a telemetry-manipulation effect cannot also falsify the experimental record.

process.description: Single-tank storage and pumping process with gravity outlet.

scenario.description:
Nominal process behaviour under synthetic variable demand. The hysteresis level controller cycles the pump between the band edges; demand is met continuously; the reported and true views of the process agree within transmitter noise.
This is the baseline every other result is read against. A range that cannot demonstrate a clean baseline cannot support a claim about anything else: if SCN-001 produced spurious violations, no violation in any other scenario would be interpretable.
scenario.name: Nominal operation
scenario.notes: No scenario events and therefore no ATT&CK for ICS mapping. Recording an empty mapping here is deliberate -- nominal operation corresponds to no adversary technique, and saying so is more useful than inventing an association.
scenario.research_question: What does correct operation look like, and does the instrument suite report zero invariant violations and zero consequence when nothing is wrong?
